proof:
Source: step 0 of the parent proof ("for every constant β and admissible g, ∫_{Q₁} β div g = 0"), with the integration along lines written as an integration by parts on ℝⁿ. In Simon this is the fact, implicit in displays (29)–(30) of the proof of Ch. 6, 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1862–1876), that subtracting the constant multiple β[[F]] does not change the boundary inside F̊.

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). Integrals over a set are Lebesgue (Bochner) integrals of the restricted measure. Under the measure-preserving linear isometry Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp / PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ), so vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded; for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ, Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let g be C¹ with compact support K := tsupport g ⊆ Q₁.

1. Regularity. Dg : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) is continuous (g is C¹), and Dg(x) = 0 for x ∉ K: such an x has the open neighbourhood ℝⁿ ∖ K on which g ≡ 0, so g is locally constant at x (Mathlib support_fderiv_subset: support (fderiv ℝ g) ⊆ tsupport g). Hence for every fixed h ∈ ℝⁿ the map x ↦ Dg(x)h is continuous with support in the compact set K, so it is integrable on ℝⁿ; likewise g is continuous with compact support, hence integrable. The map A ↦ trace A is linear on the finite-dimensional space L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), hence continuous, so x ↦ div g(x) is continuous, vanishes outside K and is integrable on ℝⁿ.

2. Directional derivatives integrate to zero. Fix h ∈ ℝⁿ. Apply integration by parts on ℝⁿ (Mathlib integral_smul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_smul_of_integrable, Lebesgue measure on Euclid n) to the scalar function f ≡ 1 and the vector function g in the direction h. Its hypotheses hold: x ↦ Df(x)h • g(x) = 0 is integrable, x ↦ f(x) • Dg(x)h = Dg(x)h is integrable by 1, x ↦ f(x) • g(x) = g(x) is integrable by 1, f is differentiable everywhere and g is differentiable everywhere (C¹). It gives ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)h dx = −∫_{ℝⁿ} Df(x)h • g(x) dx = −∫ 0 = 0. Import note: this lemma is in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts, which is not in the import closure of the frozen GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean; add `import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts` to Submission.lean (accepted nodes of this run add Mathlib imports in the same way). Alternative route inside the closure, needed only for h = e_i in step 3: identify Euclid n with Fin n → ℝ (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) and split off coordinate i (MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove, x = Fin.insertNth i t x'); by Fubini ∫_{ℝⁿ} ∂_i g_k = ∫_{x'} (∫_ℝ (d/dt) g_k(Fin.insertNth i t x') dt) dx', and for each x' the inner integral vanishes by MeasureTheory.integral_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrable (t ↦ g_k(Fin.insertNth i t x') is C¹ with compact support, so it and its derivative are integrable on ℝ).

3. Trace in the standard basis. Let e_1, …, e_n be the standard orthonormal basis of Euclid n. For every linear T : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, trace T = Σ_i ⟨e_i, T e_i⟩ (Mathlib LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner with EuclideanSpace.basisFun). Hence div g(x) = Σ_i ⟨e_i, Dg(x)e_i⟩ for every x. Since v ↦ ⟨e_i, v⟩ is a continuous linear functional and x ↦ Dg(x)e_i is integrable, ∫_{ℝⁿ} ⟨e_i, Dg(x)e_i⟩ dx = ⟨e_i, ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)e_i dx⟩ = ⟨e_i, 0⟩ = 0 by step 2. Summing over i: ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g = 0.

4. Restriction to Q₁. By step 1, div g vanishes outside K ⊆ Q₁, so the integrand of ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g vanishes off Q₁ and ∫_{Q₁} div g = ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). By step 3 this is 0. ∎
